inspiration: Reaction fire is an interrupt chain: when a unit acts, enemies that can see it are asked to shoot first. The best-scoring reactor goes first; if it cannot react it is dropped and the next is tried, until the actor is reached (src/Battlescape/TileEngine.cpp:836-861). Fits guard, parry and overwatch in a many-vs-one fight.

A reaction costs the same action points as the matching action and sends a hostile unit into an aggro state (src/Battlescape/TileEngine.cpp:1055 and 1061). An interrupt that also flips the enemy's state is readable to the player.
Reactions only trigger on actions of the side whose turn it is (src/Battlescape/TileEngine.cpp:830-831). A simple gate that keeps the interrupt chain from firing on the wrong turn.

Damage is scaled by the armour's per-damage-type multiplier before anything else (src/Savegame/BattleUnit.cpp:1106). Each armour row has a 10-entry multiplier list (bin/standard/xcom2/armors.rul, damageModifier block of the first row). A creature with a damage-type matrix, not one armour number.
Armour has four facings (front, side, rear, under) with separate values (bin/standard/xcom2/armors.rul:7-10). Armour depends on where the hit comes from, which suits a fight camera that shows facing.
Each unit row has 11 stats plus rank and race, and a stand and a kneel height (bin/standard/xcom2/units.rul:46-63). A two-pose silhouette gives a clear low-profile read.

Projectile art comes as a strip per environment, the same 110 x 33 px size for land and underwater (bin/standard/xcom2/Resources/BulletSprites/TFTD-LAND.png, TFTD-UNDERWATER.png). Projectile variants by zone with one shared size.
Soldier names come from weighted look lists per nationality (common/SoldierName/*.nam, weights at Bulgarian.nam:1). Look-weighted name and face variety for NPCs.
A menu of screen-filter shaders (bin/common/Shaders/) gives a choice of CRT, scanline and bloom looks. Useful for the colour-grade row, but only public-domain or GPL-terms ones.

briefs.label: watch-interrupt flash
briefs.why: A reaction shot is a readable interrupt: a brief cue tells the player an enemy has struck first. Silhouette-level read at 375 px: one tick and one flash, not a full effect.
keep: an interrupt before the actor's action resolves
best-scoring responder goes first, with fall-through to the next
a state flip (aggro) that the player can read
change: cue is a short colour tick on the enemy's weapon hand, not a shot
interrupt picks the nearest guard, not a score list
one signature sound of our own

briefs.label: tide-and-land projectile set
briefs.why: The same projectile strip per environment, same size, so zones change the look of a hit without new code. Works as a zone-variant effect.
keep: one shared projectile size for every zone
change: variant set by zone tint and trail, not a bubble trail
frame count per zone chosen by us
no donor art; we draw from scratch

briefs.label: plated armour by facing
briefs.why: Armour that changes with the direction of the hit gives the player a reason to move around the enemy. The table gives four facing values per armour row.
keep: in the first armour row the front value is above side and rear (armors.rul:7-9)
change: facing values per creature, not per suit
a shield-like front that ramps with stance
no donor numbers; ours tuned on our own curve

briefs.label: low-profile crouch silhouette
briefs.why: Two body heights, one for stand and one for kneel, give a crouch that lowers the hit area. Simple, readable at 375 px, and cheap to draw.
keep: stand and kneel heights in the unit row
a crouch that changes the hit silhouette
same stat block for both poses
change: crouch is a dodge pose with a short stagger, not a kneel shot
heights scaled to our creature proportions
no donor body shape; ours is a different build
